study.title: Potential scalp acupuncture and brain stimulation targets for common neurological disorders: evidence from neuroimaging studies
study.study_design: Systematic coordinate-based neuroimaging meta-analysis using Neurosynth Compose platform; not a clinical trial
study.population: Patients diagnosed with neurological disorders: SCD, MCI, AD, PD, MSA, PPA, PSA, Dyslexia, Chronic Pain, DoC; data sourced from published neuroimaging studies
study.disease_condition: Subjective Cognitive Decline (SCD), Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI), Alzheimer's Disease (AD), Parkinson's Disease (PD), Multiple System Atrophy (MSA), Primary Progressive Aphasia (PPA), Post-Stroke Aphasia (PSA), Dyslexia, Chronic Pain, Disorders of Consciousness (DoC)
study.inclusion_criteria: (1) Studies involving participants diagnosed with the targeted neurological disorders; (2) Comparisons between patient groups and healthy controls, or between treatment and control groups for the targeted disorders; (3) Utilized neuroimaging modalities such as MRI, PET, SPECT, ASL, EEG, or MEG; (4) Reported 3D Talairach or MNI coordinates for between-group comparisons.
study.exclusion_criteria: (1) Studies including only healthy participants and focusing on experimental models of neurological symptoms; (2) Research unrelated to the targeted neurological disorders, or where the disorder of interest is not the primary focus (e.g., secondary symptoms or comorbid conditions overshadowing the primary disorder); (3) Studies that do not provide standard space coordinates for analysis; (4) Neuroimaging studies conducted on non-human subjects; (5) Machine learning studies aimed at predicting treatment response rather than exploring neuroimaging findings; (6) Neuroimaging meta-analyses, reviews, or single case reports.

interventions.anatomical_location_exact: Scalp, targeting cortical surface regions within 2.5 cm of the scalp
interventions.needle_size_exact: 0.25 mm or 0.30 mm diameter, 40 mm or 50 mm length
interventions.penetration_exact: needle insertion performed at a 15-30° angle parallel to the scalp
interventions.depth_exact: 1-3 cm into the subcutaneous layer of the galea aponeurotica
interventions.manipulation_exact: twisting at 200 rotations per minute for 2-3 min; electroacupuncture may be applied per GB/T 21709.11 standards
interventions.treatment_rationale_given_exact: Neuroimaging-guided identification of cortical surface targets projected onto scalp acupuncture lines; stimulation of corresponding cortical regions to influence neural pathways and brain function

neuroimaging_methods.analysis_software_exact: Neurosynth Compose (https://compose.neurosynth.org); NiMARE; xjView toolbox (http://www.alivelearn.net/xjview/); Surf Ice (www.nitrc.org/projects/surfce/); MRIcroGL (www.mccauslandcenter.sc.edu/mricrogl/)
primary_neuroimaging_metrics: coordinate-based meta-analysis uniformity test map T-values
statistical_thresholds_exact: FDR correction with a 0.05 criterion applied to adjust the t-values in the uniformity test map for each disease
T values increased in increments of 0.5 until 3 to 9 clusters are identified with voxel counts exceeding 30 and remaining under approximately 800 across all clusters
standard cortical brain template (within 2.5 cm of the scalp) applied to identify cortically accessible brain areas
neuroimaging_methods.multiple_comparison_correction_exact: False discovery rate (FDR) correction with a 0.05 criterion

funding_conflicts_registration.conflict_of_interest_exact: JK has a disclosure to report (Holding equity in Startup companies (MNT and BTT), a granted patent and several pending patents), but declare no conflict of interest. The authors declare that they have no competing interests.
funding_conflicts_registration.data_availability_exact: The datasets generated and analyzed for this study are available in the Neurosynth Compose neuroimaging literature analysis platform repository. Links to the datasets and images for each disease mentioned in the article are provided in Table 1.

extraction_notes.note: This is a neuroimaging meta-analysis, not a clinical trial. No participants were directly enrolled, randomized, or treated. The 'n_analyzed' values in contrast entries refer to the number of included studies in each disease meta-analysis, not individual participants.
No sensory or interoceptive responses were measured in this study; the extraction section is empty because this is a meta-analysis of neuroimaging literature, not a direct acupuncture experiment.
No clinical or behavioral outcomes were directly measured in this study; clinical outcomes mentioned in the discussion refer to cited external studies, not original data from this paper.
No expectancy, blinding, credibility, or allocation guessing measures were assessed; this is a meta-analysis.
No adverse events were reported; this is a meta-analysis of neuroimaging studies, not a clinical intervention study.

The paper references Supplementary Tables 1-10 (additional deeper brain targets not from cortical template), Supplementary Table 11 (international/Chinese/Japanese/Korean nomenclature), and Supplementary Figs. 1A-1C (scalp acupuncture lines, acupoints, EEG 10-20 system). These supplementary materials were not provided in the PDF and their content was not extracted.

The paper references a dataset identifier for SCD as https://neurovault.org/collections/18684/ (not using the identifiers.org format used for other diseases). This is noted as an apparent difference in URL format.

The 'direction_exact' of meta-analytic clusters is not explicitly stated. The uniformity test reflects where studies consistently report activations or structural differences, but the paper does not uniformly label whether clusters reflect increases or decreases relative to controls.

The paper states that the coordinate space is MNI throughout, using the AAL3 template for labeling, but original included studies may have used Talairach coordinates that were converted prior to meta-analysis. Conversion details for individual included studies are not provided in this paper.
Table 1 reports number of included studies, but the total number of individual participants across studies is not provided for any of the ten disease meta-analyses.

Some clusters in the coordinate tables span multiple brain regions (e.g., 'R Middle Occipital Gyrus/ Angular Gyrus/ Parietal Lobule / Superior Temporal Gyrus'). The paper notes that for such clusters, separate peak coordinates are provided when they extend to different brain areas, but it is unclear whether the reported single coordinate represents the peak of the entire cluster or one of several sub-peaks.
The 'n_analyzed' value in the SCD contrast entry (54) refers to included studies, not individual subjects. Similarly for all other disease contrasts.

The paper assigns targets a notation '(2)' when they were previously studied in prior publications by the same group [refs 8, 9]. Targets without '(2)' are newly reported in the current study. This notation is preserved in brain_region_exact fields where applicable.

The paper references needle application positioning suggestions using scalp acupoints (e.g., GB14, BL8, etc.) and needle insertion directions/angles for each target in Tables 2-11. These have been captured in the interventions section but are proposals/recommendations derived from this meta-analysis, not interventions tested in an experiment.

Table 10, target CP(2)-1: the 'Corresponding brain area' column shows 'R Superior Frontal Gyrus' without the DLPFC parenthetical unlike other superior frontal gyrus entries (CP(2)-2 has 'PFC including DLPFC'). This may reflect different sub-regions or an omission in the original paper; preserved as written.
